Unlike many Git servers, packfiles are kept at every level and not discarded or garbage collected. Packs at every level are used to serve clients continuously, based on the     have    s and     want    s they request in a fetch. And for clients using Pando as an API, reading an arbitrary object from a packfile tends to require reading less data from an L0 than an L4, because it’s less likely to be compressed.      Compaction in Pando significantly reduces both the total transfer size sent to clients and enables pack planning to scale sub-linearly in how far behind the client is. This is especially important for large and quickly changing repositories, which we expect to be a new normal in software development.        Building Pando        We built Pando with Codex, moving from kick-off to production, in just 10 weeks. The core of Pando was designed by a single engineer, implemented by teams of agents, and deployed by a handful of engineers. Pando began serving production traffic in April of this year, and is one part of a larger system of source control management tools used at OpenAI.      We employed a wide variety of approaches when validating Pando’s design. We applied our principles for     building more secure software foundations  ⁠  . As a greenfield project, we chose to implement Pando in Rust and without legacy dependencies. We wrote a conformance test suite so agents could test their changes against standard Git behavior. We also developed deterministic simulation testing harnesses allowing us to check invariants and properties of the system, enabling us to find and mitigate subtle race conditions and regressions in negotiation and pack planning.      Many models contributed to this system; as new models became available, we used them to improve Pando’s performance and reliability. Using GPT‑6 Astra, agents wrote Lean and TLA+ to formalize a “theory of Pando” that we used to find and fix bugs in the implementation, and prove properties of the system. Multiple continuous sessions ran for hundreds of hours finding and fixing edge cases in Pando. We also run agents around the clock to red-team Git and Pando using Daybreak-capable models.        Deploying Pando        Our initial deployment of Pando was as a read- and write-through proxy to our existing source control system. This allowed us to keep Pando and the previous system in sync, so we could safely move traffic onto Pando without downtime.      As part of its caching design, Pando can also deduplicate and combine requests before proxying. This allowed us to keep our existing tools healthy as we moved systems to Pando one at a time. As we migrated more workloads to Pando, their pushes populated Pando’s cache and improved the reliability of our previous backend.      In order to optimize performance when using Pando, we began shipping our public distribution of Git to developer machines and within the ChatGPT desktop app. To migrate clients to Pando, we used an internal wrapper around the Git CLI to migrate clients in phases. We created many other tools for handling change requests, code review, and APIs for automations. We migrated hundreds of integrations that depended on legacy APIs, webhooks, and repository downloads alongside Git traffic.      Codex itself helped developers and teams make the move. We created skills for preparing existing checkouts, and for guiding agents to use the new system. As a result, developers could simply ask Codex to migrate their development environments and services.      Switching to Pando improved merge reliability and reduced the latency of the median push by nearly 80%.                Pando can deliver a petabyte of Git data per day with just a handful of CPU cores. Pando has served more than 57 terabytes of Git packs in a single hour, with more than 99% of those bytes from local disk cache.                Reusing packs lets many clients download the same repository history with little computation on the serving nodes. This example shows a single repository, but Pando is designed to support many more. As demand grows, we can scale data delivery and Git negotiation independently.        Contributing back to the Git project        Building Pando on the Git protocol and client helped us identify bugs and opportunities to improve Git’s own performance.      For example, Pando serves reusable packs directly to clients, so downloading and indexing those packs became a central part of making the system fast and reliable. That work surfaced edge cases in concurrent downloads, cleanup after interrupted transfers, and resuming downloads that had already completed. We fixed those paths, added validations when accepting an existing pack for a fetch, and contributed that work back upstream.      We also needed to see where time and bandwidth were going, so we added tracing for     packfile-uri     downloads and byte counts for pack generation, making it easier to tell whether a slow fetch was spending its time generating packs or transferring them.      In     OpenAI’s Git build  ⁠ (opens in a new window)   , the client can download and index independent packs in parallel. We added the concept of “explicit haves” so a server can advertise a branch’s current tip separately from the history a pushing client may leave out of its pack. On Pando, this enables clients to use     --force-with-lease     to check that a feature branch hasn’t moved and build its pack against trunk alone. Anyone with that trunk history can then fetch the branch using the same pack.      Several of these improvements are already in upstream Git, and many others in our public repository. We’re continuing to work with the Git community to make these improvements useful beyond Pando. You can follow that work in our     public patch tracker  ⁠ (opens in a new window)   .        What’s next        By rethinking conventional wisdom on how to scale Git repositories, Pando enables us to scale our monorepo without changing the Git workflows our engineers and agents already use. In our monorepo, Pando has unlocked a greater degree of parallelism, improved merge reliability, and reduced the time it takes to publish code changes. Beyond our monorepo, we’re also exploring other uses for Pando within OpenAI, including workloads where large numbers of agents need to collaborate on a shared Git repository.      As engineers and agents produce more software, more teams beyond OpenAI will encounter the limits we hit in source control. We’re currently exploring ways to share the technology that makes Pando possible with our users.      Pando builds on two decades of experience from users and operators of Git repositories. We’ll continue to develop Pando while working with the open-source Git community to share any improvements that benefit Git users more broadly.            2026    Codex      Author  OpenAI         Keep reading   View all                     Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users (Part II)   Engineering   Oct 23, 2026                       How we built ChatGPT’s novel ad stack for user trust and relevance   Engineering   Oct 21, 2026                       Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users   Engineering   Sep 11, 2026                     Research    Research Index    Research Overview    Economic Research      Latest Advancements    GPT-6.1 Sol    GPT-6 Astra    GPT-5.6    GPT-5.5      Safety    Safety Approach    Deployment Safety  (opens in a new window)     Security & Privacy    Trust & Transparency        Products    ChatGPT  (opens in a new window)     ChatGPT Business  (opens in a new window)     ChatGPT Enterprise  (opens in a new window)     ChatGPT for Education  (opens in a new window)     Codex    Dots  (opens in a new window)     Release Notes      API Platform    Overview    API Log In  (opens in a new window)     Docs  (opens in a new window)         Business    Overview    Solutions    Resources    Plugins    Customer Stories    Partner Network    Contact Sales      Developers    Plugins  (opens in a new window)     Models  (opens in a new window)     Docs  (opens in a new window)     Resources  (opens in a new window)     Developer Forum  (opens in a new window)         Company    About Us    Our Charter    Careers    News      Support    Help Center  (opens in a new window)     OpenAI Status  (opens in a new window)         More    Stories    Academy    Supply Co. Loading…            Share                OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. For the more than one billion people who currently use ChatGPT every week, we want to build AI that can help with the practical challenges of everyday life, like finding childcare, accessing government services, creating a budget, preparing for school, modifying recipes, ordering groceries, designing workout plans, and more.      When someone is looking for help making their life easier, they need more than advice or a chat response. To be a truly helpful personal assistant, ChatGPT should be able to take actions that actually get things done.                          To measure model performance over time on everyday tasks, we built an evaluation of tasks covering areas where users wanted the most help from AI and personal agents. We used this evaluation to track and drive improvement in model performance on everyday tasks over the past year.                   Background        To identify the tasks people value most, we started with two large studies that track how people spend time in both the U.S. and internationally: the     American Time Use Survey  ⁠ (opens in a new window)    and the     Multinational Time Use Study  ⁠ (opens in a new window)   . Together, these datasets provide a detailed catalog of everyday life tasks that people do across different demographics, times of day, and seasons. To understand where people would most value AI assistance, we expanded on these existing surveys with a new demographically representative survey of 3,995 respondents. For each task, we asked a variety of questions to identify the areas where everyday people most wanted help from a personal assistant. The resulting tasks span the most important areas that people want help with, including caregiving, health, education, household administration, personal finances, shopping, and accessing government services.         Individual task examples  Below are some examples of how our current models perform on practical workflows from everyday life.                  Enroll in the right kindergarten after moving  93.1%           Compare kindergartens near our new home and shortlist the best fits.   I’ve narrowed it to three kindergartens and organized the enrollment details. Two preferences still need your call. Want to review the shortlist?          Manage volunteers ahead of a flood  98.0%           Help me organize our community’s flood preparation volunteer force for four neighbors needing floodproofing assistance.   I’ve prepared a simple action plan to help volunteers assess the sites mentioned and help them prepare for upcoming severe weather.          Find a new home for my family  100%           Find a home in Luzerne County that fits my budget, has a separate living unit, and keeps my commute short after school drop-off. Add the deed to my cart so I can review it.   I found one home that meets your requirements. I’ve calculated the transfer tax and added the deed to your country records cart to review.          Watch a game with grandma from far away  96.3%           Set up an easy way for grandma and me to watch the game together remotely.   The easiest watch setup is ready, with a backup if the stream fails. Want me to walk you through it with grandma?          Meal prep for a parent adjusting to a new diabetes diagnosis  90.4%           Help my parent adjust to a new diabetes diagnosis with a practical care and meal plan.   The first-week plan is ready, including meals, reminders, and questions for the care team. Want to review it together before you share it with your parent?            Our latest models score very highly on many LifeVal tasks.      See more                    Over the past year, we’ve trained our models to become much faster, more capable, and more aligned on browser use, computer use, and connectors tasks. Enabling these capabilities in ChatGPT also expands the types of tasks the model can help with, helping move ChatGPT beyond a chat tool and towards a truly agentic personal assistant.               Why this matters          To ensure AGI benefits all of humanity, we need to measure and improve model progress on what matters in the lives of everyday people. That means going beyond academic assessments of model knowledge and actually measuring how well AI models can help people navigate decisions, manage everyday responsibilities, and get meaningful things done. We are hopeful that LifeVal represents a step towards that goal.                                                                                        2026      Author  OpenAI         Keep reading   View all                     How we detect frontier model misalignment   Security   Oct 29, 2026                       Working with academic communities to build scientific understanding   Research   Oct 26, 2026                       ChatGPT’s expanding world of work   Research   Oct 26, 2026                     Research    Research Index    Research Overview    Economic Research      Latest Advancements    GPT-6.1 Sol    GPT-6 Astra    GPT-5.6    GPT-5.5      Safety    Safety Approach    Deployment Safety  (opens in a new window)     Security & Privacy    Trust & Transparency        Products    ChatGPT  (opens in a new window)     ChatGPT Business  (opens in a new window)     ChatGPT Enterprise  (opens in a new window)     ChatGPT for Education  (opens in a new window)     Codex    Dots  (opens in a new window)     Release Notes      API Platform    Overview    API Log In  (opens in a new window)     Docs  (opens in a new window)         Business    Overview    Solutions    Resources    Plugins    Customer Stories    Partner Network    Contact Sales      Developers    Plugins  (opens in a new window)     Models  (opens in a new window)     Docs  (opens in a new window)     Resources  (opens in a new window)     Developer Forum  (opens in a new window)         Company    About Us    Our Charter    Careers    News      Support    Help Center  (opens in a new window)     OpenAI Status  (opens in a new window)         More    Stories    Academy    Supply Co. Netpbm.

CHANGE HISTORY 
--------------

26.09.28 BJH  Release 10.86.51

              pamtogif: fix spurious memory reference and incorrect output
              when input image has an alpha channel.  Always broken (pamtogif
              was new in Netpbm 10.37 (December 2006)).

              pamtogif: fix spurious memory reference and incorrect output
              when input image has a nonstandard visual image tuple type.
              Always broken (pamtogif was new in Netpbm 10.37 (December
              2006)).

              pnmtojbig: fix incorrect output with PGM input with maxval >
              255.  Always broken (pnmtojbig was new in Netpbm 9.2 (May
              2000)).

              pnmtojbig: fix incorrect output with PGM input with width *
              length * bytes per pixel > 32 bits.  Always broken (pnmtojbig
              was new in Netpbm 9.2 (May 2000)).

              jbigtopnm: fix buffer overrun with ridiculously large input
              image.  Always broken (jbigtopnm was new in Netpbm 9.2
              (May 2000)).  Discovered and diagnosed by Tristan Madani.

              jbigtopnm: fix incorrect output with maxval > 255.  Always
              broken (jbigtopnm was new in Netpbm 9.2 (May 2000)).
              
              jbigtopnm: fix invalid memory write when memory allocation
              fails.  Always broken (jbigtopnm was new in Netpbm 9.2 (May
              2000)).
              
              picttoppm: fix buffer overrun with very large polygons in input.
              Always broken -- in fact done intentionally for coding
              convenience (picttoppm was in primordial Netpbm in 1988).
              Discovered and diagnosed by Tristan Madani.

              tgatoppm: fix buffer overrun with corrupted Targa input.  Fail
              if Targa image contains invalid color index.  Always broken
              (tgatoppm was in primordial Netpm in 1989).  Discovered and
              diagnosed by Tristan Madani.

              winicontopam: fix arithmetic overflow causing arbitrary memory
              access and infinite loops with large images.  Always broken
              (winicontopam was new in Netpbm 10.63 (June 2013).  Discovered
              and diagnosed by Tristan Madani.

              xpmtoppm: fix buffer overruns with input image that has an
              invalid characters-per-pixel value.  Always broken (xpmtoppm was
              in primordial Netpbm in 1994).  Discovered and diagnosed by
              Tristan Madani.

              sgitopnm: fix buffer overrun with corrupted RLE input.  Always
              broken (sgitopnm was in primordial Netpbm in 1994).

              pbmtomda: fix incorrect output (invalid image) with -dscale.
              Always broken (pbmtomda was new in Netpbm 9.1 (May 2000)).

              mdatopbm: fix failure when height or width of MDA is 2^15 or
              more.  Always broken (mdatopbm was new in Netpbm 9.1 (May 2000)).

              mrftopbm: fix crash with zero width or height in MRF header.
              Always broken (mrftopbm was new in Netpbm 10.18 (March 2009)).

              pjtoppm: fix write to arbitrary memory after a position command.
              Always broken (pjtoppm was in primordial Netpbm, 1991).

              pjtoppm: fix crash due to spurious memory access with compressed
              (mode 1) input.  Always broken (pjtoppm was in primordial
              Netpbm, 1991).
              
              winicontopam: fix incorrect message saying all pixels in the
              transparency map are fully transparent when there is no
              transparency map.  Introduced in Netpbm 10.92 (September 2020).

              pamtowinicon: fix incorrect icon directory entry for an image
              that is BMP truecolor, but only because it would be larger as a
              paletted BMP.  Always broken (pamtowinicon was new in Netpbm
              10.63 (June 2013).

              pgmtexture: fix incorrect max correlation coefficient output.
              Always broken (pgmtexture was in primordial Netpbm in 1991).

              pgmtexture: fix invalid memory reference when image is all a
              single shade of gray.  Always broken (pgmtexture was in
              primordial Netpbm in 1991).

              thinkjettopbm: fix failure when input is from Standard Input.
              Introduced in Netpbm 10.12 (November 2002).

              lispmtopgm: fix too-dim output (because maxval is too big).
              Always broken (lispmtopgm was in primordial Netpbm).

              lispmtopgm: fix incorrect output when width not a multiple of
              32.  Always broken (lispmtopgm was in primordial Netpbm).

              imgtoppm: fix write to arbitrary memory with invalid input
              (excessively long variable length field).  Always broken.
              (imgtoppm was in primordial Netpbm).

              build: fix omission of 'pbm_dumpfont' from libnetpbm.  Broken in
              Netpbm 10.84 (September 2018).

26.06.27 BJH  Release 10.86.50

              pamcut: fix incorrect behavior or crash with options that
              specify an uncomputably large column or row number (UINT_MAX).

              pbmtopgm: fix incorrect output with absurdly large convolution
              kernel.

              ppmtopict: fix incorrect output with oversize input image.

              pnmtojbig: fix empty output when input image is large.
              Always broken (pnmtojbig was new in Netpbm 9.2 (May 2000)).

26.03.31 BJH  Release 10.86.49

              pcxtoppm: fix determination that palette in image is all one
              color (so probably in error) based on random memory access.
              Always broken (all-one-color feature was added in July 1995).

              pbmtext: fix crash when input text contains a character with
              code >127.  Broken in Netpbm 10.82 (March 2018).

              pnmhisteq: fix incorrect output with -gray: color pixels
              changed, gray pixels left alone.  Broken in Netpbm 10.30
              (October 2005).

              asciitopgm: fix crash with missing height or width argument.
              Always broken (asciitopgm was new in the 1994 Netpbm release).

              asciitopgm: fix crash with zero divisor.
              Always broken (asciitopgm was new in the 1994 Netpbm release).

25.09.27 BJH  Release 10.86.48

              pamtris: fix unrecognized command or crash on line with no
              command.  Broken in Netpbm 10.85 (December 2018).

              ppmcmap.h: fix C++ compilation.  Broken at least since Netpbm
              10.35 (August 2006).

25.06.28 BJH  Release 10.86.47

              pnmquantall: Fix vestigial temp file when program fails.
              Introduced in Netpbm 10.86.46 (April 2025).

              libnetpbm ppmd_fill and ppmdraw filled shapes: fix bug: final
              span of filling omitted from output.  Always broken (ppmd_fill
              was in primordial Netpbm).

              pamdice: fix using more digits than necessary in output file
              names -- width was based on one more slice than was actually
              generated.  Broken since Netpbm 10.29 (August 2005).

              pnmtofiasco: fix bug: infinite loop with multiple tiles.
              Always broken (program was new in Netpbm 9.6, July 2000),
              but made functional by bug fix in 10.86.46 (April 2025).

25.04.07 BJH  Release 10.86.46

              pnmquantall: fix arbitrary shell command execution with input
              file names or color count that contain shell metacharacters.
              Always present ('pnmquantall' has existed, aka 'ppmquantall',
              since primordial Netpbm).

              ppmtogif: fix arbitrary shell commands when arguments contain
              shell metacharacters.  Broken in Netpbm 10.37 (June 2006).

              pnmtofiasco: fix crash when image is really small.  Always
              broken (programs were new in Netpbm 9.6, July 2000).
              
              pnmtofiasco: fix bug: uses one tile regardless of
              --tiling-exponent.  Always broken (programs were new in Netpbm
              9.6, July 2000).

25.03.28 BJH  Release 10.86.45

              giftopnm: Fix wild pointer reference with -verbose and
              invalid extension type.  Broken in Netpbm 10.59 (December 2012).

              pdbimgtopam, pamtopdbimg: Fix crash when out of memory.  Always
              broken (programs were new in Netpbm 10.52 (September 2010)).

24.12.25 BJH  Release 10.86.44

              pbmtoascii: fix bug: allows both -1x2 and -2x4.  Always present
              (pbmtoascii existed in primordial Netpbm).

24.09.29 BJH  Release 10.86.43

              libnetpbm color name parsing: Fix handling of rgb: color names
              with more than 4 hex digits per plane, so it throws an error
              instead of generating an invalid or wrong color.  Broken in
              primordial Netpbm.

              libnetpbm color name parsing: Fix error message for invalid
              rgb-  color name.

24.06.28 BJH  Release 10.86.42

              libnetpbm: Fix double free crash when memory allocation via
              REALLOCARRAY fails.  Introduced in Netpbm 10.40 (September
              2007).

24.03.30 BJH  Release 10.86.41

              infotopam: fix incorrect output -- columns always in wrong
              place.  Always broken.  (infotopam was new in Netpbm 10.22 (May
              2004)).

23.12.28 BJH  Release 10.86.40

              pnmconvol: Restore ability of convolution matrix to be a
              pseudo-plain-PNM with samples that exceed the maxval.  Lost in
              10.30 (October 2005) because maxval-checking code was added to
              libnetpbm.  (Was fixed in 10.47.08 in November 2010, but only in
              the 10.47 series).

              pnmpad: fix wrong results with old-style options (e.g. "-t50").

              pnmpad: fix behavior with -left, -right, and -width together or
              -top, -bottom, -height together: ignores -width where it should
              fail.  Broken in Netpbm 10.72 (September 2015).

23.09.27 BJH  Release 10.86.39

              pamtosvg: fix hang.

              pamstack: Fail gracefully when total number of planes is too
              large for unsigned integer.  Always broken (Pamstack was new in
              Netpbm 10.0 (June 2002).

              pgmtexture: Fix buffer overflow with maxval > 255.  Always
              broken.  Maxvals > 255 were possible starting in Netpbm 9.0
              (April 2000).

              ppmrough: fix buffer overrun.  Always broken (Ppmrough was new
              in Netpbm 10.9 (September 2002).

              pbmtoxbm: Fix spurious output with really wide rows.

23.03.25 BJH  Release 10.86.38

              jpegtopnm: Many fixes to -dumpexif.  Always broken.
              (-dumpexif was new in Netpbm 9.18 (September 2001))

23.03.14 BJH  Release 10.86.37

              pamtopng: fix -chroma option: always rejected.  Always broken.
              pamtopng was new in Netpbm 10.70 (June 2015).

              pnmtopng: fix -rgb option: always rejected.  Always broken
              -rgb was new in Netpbm 10.30 (October 2005).

22.12.24 BJH  Release 10.86.36

              ppmtompeg: Fix crash with resize option because of invalid
              memory free.

              fitstopnm: fix invalid memory reference (nonterminated ASCIIZ
              string).

22.09.24 BJH  Release 10.86.35

              pnmindex: fix shell injection vulnerabilities.  Broken since
              Netpbm 10.28 (June 2005).

              pnmmargin: fix shell injection vulneraibility.  Always broken
              (Program was added in primordial Netpbm in 1990).

22.07.17 BJH  Release 10.86.34

              ppmtoicr: Fix bug: all options cause bogus command line parsing
              errors.  Always broken.  Ppmtoicr was new in 1991.

              ppmtoicr: Fix arithmetic overflows.

              ppmtoicr: make -rle option issue an error message saying it no
              longer exists (it did, sort of, before 2015).

              palmtopnm: Fix failure with bogus claim of invalid input on
              architectures that do not use two's complement negative numbers.
              Always broken.  (Ability to convert PackBits input was new in
              Netpbm 10.27 (March 2005).

              pnmgamma -srgbtobt709, -bt709tosrgb: fix bug; incorrect output.
              Always broken (These options were new in Netpbm 10.32 (February
              2006)).  Thanks Alexander Shpilkin  .

              pamdice: Fix incorrect output file name with PAM input.  Always
              broken (pamdice was new in Netpbm 9.25 (March 2002).

22.03.20 BJH  Release 10.86.32

              pamx: Fix bug: top-justifies image in all cases where it should
              bottom-justify.  Always broken.  (pamx was new in Netpbm 10.34
              (June 2006).

              pnmtorle: Fix bug: -h works only on first image.

              pamsistoaglyph: Fix invalid memory reference and incorrect
              output on depth 1 input.  Always broken.  (pamsistoaglyph was
              new in Netpbm 10.47 (June 2009).  Thanks Scott Pakin.

              pambayer: Fix bogus colors at edges.  Always broken (pambayer
              was new in Release 10.30 (October 2005)).

22.02.13 BJH  Release 10.86.31

              libnetpbm, various programs: fix bug: bogus warning that a color
              specified on command line cannot be represented exactly with the
              maxval being used.  Introduced in Netpbm 10.83 (June 2018).

              ppmtoapplevol: Fix bug: reads from Standard Input even when you
              specify the input file argument.  Always broken.  (ppmtoapplevol
              was new in Netpbm 10.54 (March 2011).

              ppmtoapplevol: Fix bug: produces garbage with input image wider
              than 255.  Always broken.  (ppmtoapplevol was new in Netpbm
              10.54 (March 2011).

22.01.25 BJH  Release 10.86.30

              pgmabel: Fix incorrect output.  Always broken.  (Program was
              new in Netpbm 10.3 (July 2002).

              libnetpbm: Fix version number

22.01.24 BJH  Release 10.86.29

              picttoppm:  Fix inability to compile introduced in Netpbm
              10.86.28 (2 days ago).

22.01.22 BJH  Release 10.86.28
 
              picttoppm: Fix incorrect output for 32 bit per pixel images
              that have only 3 planes.  Broken in Netpbm 10.34 (June 2006).

              pamendian: fix bogus "sample exceeds maxval" failure.
              Introduced in Netpbm 10.66 (March 2014).

              ppmtoilbm: Fix wild memory references and hangs with -map .
              Introduced in Netpbm 9.12 (March 2001).

              pgmtexture: Fix incorrect output.  Always broken.  (Program was
              added in primordial Netpbm in 1991).
              
21.11.28 BJH  Release 10.86.27

              palmtopnm: Fix bug: fails with PackBits input on platform with
              default unsigned char, such as ppc64.  Always broken.  (Ability
              to convert PackBits input was new in Netpbm 10.27 (March 2005).
              
21.11.19 BJH  Release 10.86.26

              pamrubber: Fix bug: random behavior with -quad when you specify
              both points for source or target and the second one is lower in
              the image than the first.  Always broken (Pamrubber was new in
              Netpbm 10.54 (March 2011)).

              sunicontopnm, escp2topbm, mgrtopbm, ybmtopbm, pamcut, pbmpscale,
              pnmcat, pnmpad: Fix arithmetic overrun with ridiculously large
              image.

21.10.17 BJH  Release 10.86.25

              pamtogif: Fix bug: doesn't ignore the input alpha mask when user
              specified -transparent.  Broken in Netpbm 10.37 (December 2006).

              libnetpbm: When validating computable size of width and height,
              allow for adding up to 10 instead of 2, to account for rounding
              up to a multiple of 8 in processing bit maps.

21.08.30 BJH  Release 10.86.24

              ximtoppm: Fix bug: invalid memory references with pathological
              image input.  Broken in Netpbm 86.15 (June 2020).

21.06.30 BJH  Release 10.86.23

              pamtopng: Fix -transparent option - program recognized
              -transparency instead.  Always broken (pamtopng was new in
              Netpbm 10.71 (June 2015)).

              Build: make it work on systems that don't have date +%s.  Broken
              in Netpbm 10.78 (March 2017).  Thanks Claes Nästén
              (pekdon@gmail.com).

21.05.15 BJH  Release 10.86.22

              pamtopng: Fix rejection of all BLACKANDWHITE_ALPHA images with
              message about wrong depth.  Always broken (pamtopng was new in
              Netpbm 10.71 (June 2015)).  Thanks Karol Kosek
               .

              pamtopng: Fix failure with GRAYSCALE_ALPHA images with maxval

              pamtopng: Fix: treats all tuple types that start with BLA as

              pamtogif: Fix failure with bogus message about wrong depth with

giftopnm        Replaces giftoppm. Examines the input image and produces
                a pbm, pgm, or ppm output.

pstopnm         Convert PostScript to pnm. Requires Ghostscript.

zeisstopnm      Conversion utility for files created by Zeiss confocal
                microscopes (the old standard).

pnmalias        Anti aliasing filter.

pnmcomp         Composite two portable anymaps together.

pnmcrop         New options added.

pnmpad          Add borders to anymap.


LIBTIFF

A new release of libtiff is included. Please read its supporting
documentation.


CHANGE LOG FROM PBMPLUS
-----------------------

Changes since the 30oct91 patch version:

    Fixed uninitialized variable in ppmtotga.  (John Walker)
    Added pgmcrater, ppmforge, ppmtoacad, sldtoppm.  (John Walker)
    Slight change to the p?mmerge.c front-ends to allow for main programs
      that return instead of exitting.
    Minor clarifications to the pnmconvol man page.
    Fixed xwdtopnm to read some 16-bit True/Direct files. (David Elliott)
    Fixed uninitialized variables in pnmtotiff.  (Larry Rosenstein, Bayles Holt)
    Added a couple of checks for \r while reading whitespace. (Larry Rosenstein)
    Removed all the BROKENPUTC stuff.  Now we ignore all return values from
      putc(), and check ferror() in pm_close().  Added pm_close() calls to
      many of the filters.
    Fixed pnmdepth to check for too-large newmaxvals.  Improved rounding
      in pnmdepth and PPM_DEPTH macro.  (Tom Lane)
    Minor fix to ppmtouil.  (Mohsen Banan)
    Added new Imakefiles.  (Rainer Klute)

Changes since the 05oct91 X11R5 contrib tape version:

    Fixed minor SysV config error in pbmplus.h.  (Tom Lane)
    Fixed tifftopnm so that BITSPERSAMPLE and SAMPLESPERPIXEL default
      correctly.  Fixed possible bug in tgatoppm line-interleaving code.
      (Arthur David Olson)
    Fixed tifftopnm so that colormapped files are read correctly.
      (PauL Drews, Mike Wade)
    Corrected use of DefaultRGBDatabase / RGB_DB for imake sites.
      (Randal L. Schwartz)
    Bugfix to pnmtops color PostScript in -rle mode.  (Angus Duggan)
    Added auto-turning to pnmtops.
    Added run-length encoding to ppmtotga.
    Space optimization to pgmoil.

Changes since the 27sep91 comp.sources.misc distribution:

    Fixed spelling error in giftoppm.  Fixed ppmrelief to not shrink the
      image by 2 rows and columns.  Minor fix to pgmramp.  Fixed off-by-one
      error in pnmtoxwd.  Man page fix for pnmgamma.  (Arthur David Olson)
    Converted ANSI trigraphs in ppmtosixel into good old octal.  (Jeff Glover)
    Fix to 24/32 bit case in rasttopnm.  (Behr de Ruiter)
    Float/double portability fix to libppm4.  (Bruce Holmer, Ronald Khoo)
    Fixed typo in compat.ksh.  (Larry Virden)
    Fixed int/short incompatibility in tifftopnm.  (Salik Rafiq)

Changes during the extended beta test period, starting on 15jan91:

    Lots of fixes from: Anthony A. Datri, Arthur David Olson, David Brooks,
      David Elliott, Doug Claar, Duncan Sinclair, Francois Pinard, Gerard
      Leurs, Jim Hanko, Ken Laprade, Klaus U. Schallhorn, Markus Bolz, Mike
      Hench, Philip Gladstone, R C Smith, Selden E. Ball, Jr., Stephen Uitti,
      Steve Allen, Tom Lane, update.kpj-jaakkola@athena.dsv.su.se,
      Charles Karney, Unmesh Agarwala, Ed Pendzik, Juha Sarlin, Tom Tulinsky,
      Phillip Smith, Lai-King Mau, David Koblas, Mark Donovan.
    Added a global -version flag.
    Added bunches of statics and prototypes.  Now compiles with zero
      warnings under gcc -ansi -pedantic.
    Changed #ifdef __STDC__ to #if __STDC__, since some non-compliant
      compilers define it as 0.
    Changed pm_message and pm_error to be varargs routines.  Added a
      portable version of vfprintf for those systems which don't have it.
    Removed the option of not compiling the pgm and ppm parts.  Very few
      people used it, and it added amazing complexity to the pnm programs,
      turning them into maintenance nightmares.
    Merged pbmpaste into pnmpaste.
    Merged pgmtops and ppmtops into pnmtops.
    Added auto-scaling and dpi / page size flags to pnmtops.
    Changed the interpretation of bits in pbmlife to conform with other
      tools.
    Changed xwdtopnm to ignore the pixel number in the xwd color structure.
    Added a -pseudodepth flag to pnmtoxwd.
    Updated tifftopnm for libtiff 2.4.
    Added many option flags to pnmtotiff.  (J.T. Conklin)
    Added recognition of X11R5's new color specifiers rgb: and rgbi:.
    Added pgmtexture.  (James Darrell McCauley)
    Added ppmtopj, pjtoppm, and ppmdither.  (Christos Zoulas)
    Added ppmtotga.  (Mark Shand)
    Added ppmtosixel.  (Rick Vinci)
    Added pbmtoatk and atktopbm.  (Bill Janssen)
    Added ppmtoyuv and yuvtoppm.  (Marc Boucher)
    Fixes to picttoppm.  (George Phillips)
    Added recognition of 24-bit images to ilbmtoppm.  (Mark Thompson)

Changes since the X.V11R4 / comp.sources.misc distribution of 22nov89:

    Added pgmramp, pgmedge, pgmtoppm, rgb3toppm, ppmtoxpm, pnmgamma,
      ximtoppm, pgmtofs, picttoppm, ppmtopict, ppmquantall, anytopnm,
      pi1toppm, ppmtopi1, sputoppm, spctoppm, pbmto10x, ppmtoicr, ppmmake,
      xpmtoppm, ppmtopuzz, ppmtouil, ybmtopbm, pbmtoybm, lispmtopgm,
      pgmtolispm, pbmtogem, pi3topbm, pbmtopi3, pbmtoepson, pbmtoplot,
      pbmtozinc, pbmtext, pnmnoraw, pnmmargin, pnmfile, pnmindex,
      ppmtorgb3, gouldtoppm, pgmbentley, pgmoil, ppmrelief, pnmtotiff,
      ppmtopcx.
    Merged some filters:
      rasttopbm and rasttoppm into rasttopnm;
      pbmtorast and ppmtorast into pnmtorast;
      xwdtopbm and xwdtoppm into xwdtopnm;
      pbmtoxwd and ppmtoxwd into pnmtoxwd.
    Promoted some filters:
      pcxtopbm to pcxtoppm;
      ppmarith to pnmarith;
      ppmconvol to pnmconvol;
      ppmcscale to pnmdepth;
      ppmrotate to pnmrotate;
      ppmscale to pnmscale;
      ppmshear to pnmshear;
      ppmsmooth to pnmsmooth;
      tifftopgm to tifftopnm - new version based on Sam Leffler's libtiff.
    Bugfixes to pbmtoicon, ppmtops.
    The Makefiles now have a "merge" option.
    All flags are now case-insensitive.
    Added $(MAKE) stuff to Makefile.
    Changed pnmsmooth from a csh script to a sh script.
    Made macro use in pbmtox10bm and pbmtoxbm more portable.
    Moved compataliases to compat.csh, and added compat.ksh.
    Made ppmtoilbm less Amiga-specific.
    Added -headerskip and -rowskip flags to rawtopgm.
    Enhanced rasttopnm to interpret 8-bit rasters with no colormap as grayscale.
    Changed sscanf %g to %f - some systems can't handle %g on input.
    Added -expand flag to pbmmask.
    Speedup to pnmflip - don't buffer if possible.
    Added color-name-to-value routine to ppm - uses X11's rgb.txt if present.
    Updated Imakefile function to reflect X.V11R4.
    Removed picttopbm.
    Improved pnmcut argument syntax so that negative coords work like pnmpaste.
    Added "magic" file, for use with the "file" program.
    40% speedup for pgmnorm from Robert Stockton (rgs@cs.cmu.edu).
    Fixed long-standing bug involving colormaps on SPARCstations when
      compiled with gcc -- had to do with passing structs by value.
    Removed the -x flag from pnmtorast -- it's not really needed.
    Fixed subtle bug in the pnm reading code that caused pnmcat to blow
      it on images that differed greatly in width or height.
    New version of giftoppm that handles the GIF89a standard, and doesn't
      use fseek.
    Fixed fitstopgm to handle three-axis images, such as the Hubble pix.
    Xwdtopnm and pnmtoxwd finally handle byte-order properly.
    Added -xysize flag to pnmscale.
    Added conditional ANSI function prototypes to library routines.
    Added -noantialias flag to pnmrotate and pnmshear.
    Removed the TIPS file.  No one ever sent in any new tips, so I just
      moved the few I had into the relevant man pages.  That's probably
      where they belonged in the first place.
    Added justification flags to pnmcat.
    Added -map flag to ppmquant - user-specifiable colormap.  Also, the
      Floyd-Steinberg error diffusion finally works right.
    Added -map flag to pgmtoppm.
    Added DirectColor capability to xwdtopnm and pnmtoxwd.
    Speedup to pgmtolj from Arthur David Olson: avoid sending whitespace.
    Fix to pbmtogo from Bo Thide': 2D compression now works.

Patch 1 to the X.V11R4 / comp.sources.misc distribution of 22nov89:

    Fixed bug in pgmtops -rle.

Changes since the alt.sources distribution of 13sep89:

    Small corrections to ppmtorast, pgmtops.
    Moved pbm/tifftopbm to pgm/tifftopgm - it now handles grayscale TIFF files.
    Fixed tifftopgm to handle non-native byte order.
    Changes to tifftopgm to handle bogus AppleScan TIFF files, to have
      better command syntax, and to use stdio.
    Optimizations to xbmtopbm, pbmtoxbm, and pbmtox10bm, courtesy of
      Juha Sarlin, to make them go about three times as fast.
    Optimization to pgmtops and ppmtops to make them go three times as fast.
    Optimization to pnmcrop.
    Added PBMPLUS_BROKENPUTC defines in pbmplus.h to handle systems (such as
      ULTRIX) which have broken putc() macros.
    Rewrote ppmscale, pnmcat, and pgmhist to operate line-by-line, instead
      of reading in the whole image.
    Rewrote pnmflip to keep only one copy of the image in memory.
    Added pgmtofits, courtesy of Wilson H. Bent, plus bugfixes to fitstopgm
      and a patch to giftoppm to handle black&white GIF files.
    Added picttopbm and rawtopgm.
    Fixes to xwdtoppm and ppmtoxwd so they compile with SunOS cc as well as gcc.
    Another small change to ppmtoxwd having to do with colormap size.
    Changed macptopbm's -headersize flag to be -extraskip.
    Changed tgatoppm to read color values as BGRA instead of ARGB; the Targa
      documentation is apparently wrong about the order.
    Some changes to the Makefiles, partially to work around bugs in gnumake.
    Got g3topbm working, and added pbmtog3, courtesy of Paul Haeberli.
    Added some pixrect work-alike code so that rasttopbm, pbmtorast, rasttoppm,
      and ppmtorast can be used on non-Sun systems.  This also provides a
      final solution to the persistent byte- and bit-order problems on 386's.
    Moved the SYSV-checking #ifdefs to *after* the include of pbm.h, which
      defines SYSV.
    Made all the #else's and #endif's ANSI-compliant.
    Added manual pages for libpbm, libpgm, libppm, and libpnm, courtesy
      of Tony Hansen.
    Changed man page installation so that pages from different sections
      can go in different directories.
    Fixed Imakefiles.

Changes since the expo.lcs.mit.edu FTP distribution of 06sep89:

    Added #ifdefs to pnm/libpnm3.c to allow the PBM-PNM-only configuration.
    Small corrections to TIPS, pnm/Makefile, pnm/Imakefile, ppm/ppmrotate.1,
      ppm/ppmshear.1, ppm/ppmtoilbm.c, pbm/xwdtopbm.c, ppm/xwdtoppm.c,
      ppm/ppmtoxwd.c, ppm/ppmtoxwd.1, pbm/x11wd.h.

Changes since the comp.sources.misc distribution of 31oct88:

    Added pbmreduce, pbmlife, pbmmask, and pbmupc.
    Added gemtopbm, tifftopbm, pcxtopbm, pbmtogo, mgrtopbm, pbmtomgr,
      cmuwmtopbm, pbmtocmuwm, g3topbm, and pbmtobg.
    Minor bugfix to pbmtolj.
    Slight restructuring of most of the programs to use vastly less memory.
    Various other minor optimizations.
    Fixed pbmtorast and rasttopbm to handle byte-swapped big-endian 386 boxes.
    Slight changes to argument syntax of pbmcrop, pbmmake, pbmreduce.
    Moved to the new PGM package: pbmtops (which now produces Conforming PS).
    Moved to the new PPM package: giftopbm.
    Moved to the new PNM package: pbmcrop pbmcut pbmenlarge pbminvert.
    Consolidated into a single pnmflip tool: pbmfliplr pbmfliptb pbmtrnspos.
    Consolidated into a single pnmcat tool: pbmcatlr pbmcattb.
    Added compataliases script for upward compatibility with changed tools.
    Removed xxxtopbm.
    Added a -headersize flag to macptopbm, to help get around annoying
      problems in MacPaint file format.
    Added the RAWBITS compilation-time option, to use a more compact and
      much faster (but less portable) external format.
    Removed the CBM format - use compress(1) and / or RAWBITS instead.
    Pbmpaste (and the new pnmpaste) now accepts negative x and y coords,
      which are interpreted relative to the right and bottom sides.
    Changed all programs to accept a "-" file argument as meaning standard
      input.
    Removed pbmtox10wd, since it was never very useful (X10 doesn't have xwud).
    Added Imakefiles, for X11 types to use.

Changes since the X.V11R3 distribution of 31aug88:

    The cbm format has been revised to include run-length encoding.
    Pbmtops now does run-length encoding.

Major changes since the X.V11R2 distribution of 28mar88:

    The pbm format now has a "magic number".
    New conversion filters: brushtopbm, giftopbm, pbmtolj, pbmtomacp,
      pbmtoxwd, and pbmtox10wd.
    Icontopbm converter has a better parser -- it knows to skip over
      any extraneous comments at the beginning of the icon file.
    Pbmtops generates a different PostScript wrapper program -- it should
      handle huge bitmaps better.
    Xwdtopbm now handles byte-swapping correctly.
    Pbmmake takes a flag to specify the color of the new bitmap.
    Pbmpaste now implements 'or', 'and', and 'xor' operations as well
      as the default 'replace'.

## CSGHub

CSGHub is an open-source platform designed for managing Large Language Models (LLM) assets, offering an efficient way to handle the entire LLM and their assets such as datasets, spaces and codes etc. It allows users to upload, download, store, verify, and distribute LLM assets like DeepSeek,Llama etc.via a web interface, `git` command line, a natural language Chatbot, or [CSGHub SDK](https://github.com/OpenCSGs/csghub-sdk).

Additionally, CSGHub features microservice submodules and standardized OpenAPIs for seamless integration with existing systems. It aims to provide a user-friendly management platform specifically for LLM, which can be deployed On-Premise for secure, offline operation. Essentially, CSGHub serves as a private, on-premise version of Huggingface.

![CSGHub](./docs/images/csghub_framework.png)

### Key Features

- Unified LLMs Management
- Extensible Development Framework
- Advanced Model Capabilities and Optimization
- Space and Asset Management Assistant (Copilot)
- Multi-Source Data Synchronization and Recommendation
- Enterprise-Level Security and Access Control
- On-Premises Deployment Solutions
- E2E Data Processing and Intelligent Annotation System
- Resilient High-Availability Architecture

For further information, please see the [detailed introduction](./docs/detailed_intro_en.md) of CSGHub.

### Demo Video

To help users get up to speed with CSGHub, we have created a demo video that highlights its key features and how it works. You can watch it below or on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6LwGQ07qBxU)/[Bilibili](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1ynmxY3EXz/).
<video width="658" height="432" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04f9fa17-9294-44c1-8c4a-4d7b9a5c66fa"></video>

### Quick Start

- For those looking to quickly explore, experiment with CSGHub's free SaaS version on the [OpenCSG website](https://opencsg.com). Refer to this [brief quick start guide](./docs/csghub_saas_en.md) to handle LLMs/datasets and deploy LLM applications with CSGHub SaaS interface.

- **For users seeking further practice:** Please refer to the [CSGHub official documentation](https://opencsg.com/docs/csghub/101/introduction). The documentation currently provides installation methods using [Docker Compose](https://opencsg.com/docs/en/csghub/101/install/docker/overview) and [Helm Chart](https://opencsg.com/docs/en/csghub/101/install/kubernetes/overview).

    _For more information and advanced tutorials, please refer to the [OpenCSG Documentation Center](https://opencsg.com/docs/intro)._


### Quick Try

[![one-click deployment on Ali marketplace](https://img.alicdn.com/imgextra/i1/O1CN01YT0adL1pi2znO6BAJ_!!6000000005393-55-tps-208-40.svg)](https://market.aliyun.com/products/56014009/cmgj00068499.html?source=5176.29345612&userCode=swc743za)

### Roadmap

Discover the [roadmap](./docs/roadmap_en.md) outlining CSGHub's future direction.

### Release Notes

Refer to [release notes](./docs/release_notes.md) for information on feature improvements.

### Meetings & Contributing

We warmly invite you to explore the [OpenCSG Community](https://github.com/OpenCSGs/community), where you'll find comprehensive guides on becoming a vital part of the project.

- The process for joining [community meetings](https://github.com/OpenCSGs/community?tab=readme-ov-file#community-meeting), where you can engage with fellow members and share your ideas.
- Refer to the [contribution guide](https://github.com/OpenCSGs/community/blob/main/guidelines/CONTRIBUTING_en.md) for strategies on how to contribute to the project.
- [Contact us](https://github.com/OpenCSGs/community?tab=readme-ov-file#questions-and-issues) for any questions or issues, ensuring you're always supported throughout your journey with OpenCSG.
- Refer to the [development guide](./docs/setup_en.md) for instructions on setting up the development environment.

                                   Security: unauthenticated private repository file disclosure via resolve handler admin-token fallback and current_user injection     #1586            New issue         Copy link           New issue         Copy link             Open              Open      Security: unauthenticated private repository file disclosure via resolve handler admin-token fallback and current_user injection   #1586             Copy link                         Description             HieuPenguinnn    opened    on Oct 31, 2026               Issue body actions          Summary 
 The CSGHub portal exposes an unauthenticated read of private repository file contents. The file resolve route  GET /:repo_type/:namespace/:name/resolve/:branch/*path  is registered with no authentication middleware, and when the request has no  user_token  cookie the portal fetches the file from the backend API using the global server API key (an administrative service credential) instead of a per-user token. On that privileged call the acting identity is carried only in a  current_user  query parameter, and the attacker-controlled file path is interpolated into the backend URL with no encoding ahead of that parameter, so a file path containing an encoded query separator overrides  current_user  with any value the attacker chooses. 
 An unauthenticated client can therefore read a private model, code, or space file belonging to another user or organization by naming the repository and injecting the owner into  current_user . For a personal repository the namespace is the owner name, so no secret or random identifier is needed. 
 Affected: v2.6.0-ce (portal  OpenCSGs/csghub ) together with  OpenCSGs/csghub-server  v2.6.0-ce. 
 Root cause (portal, OpenCSGs/csghub @ v2.6.0-ce) 
 
  internal/routes/router.go:302  registers the resolve route in a bare group with no per-route guard, unlike the upload routes just above it which use  middleware.Instance.ApiCheckCurrentUser() . 
  internal/middleware/auth_middleware.go   AuthMiddleware  does not block anonymous callers, it only sets the current user when a  login_identity  cookie is present. 
  internal/handlers/frontend/resolve.go:138  and  :146  select the service-key methods  DownloadFile  /  DownloadFileRaw  whenever the  user_token  cookie is absent (always, for an anonymous client). 
  pkg/server/backend/csghubserver/csghubserver.go:175  sends the request with  Authorization: Bearer <server api key> . 
  pkg/server/backend/csghubserver/download.go:10  and  :31  interpolate  FilePath  with  %s  ahead of  ?current_user=%s  with no  url.PathEscape  /  url.QueryEscape . Gin runs with default settings, so a percent-encoded query separator in the catch-all segment is decoded into  FilePath . A path ending with  README.md%3Fcurrent_user%3D<owner>%26  produces the backend path  /models/<owner>/<repo>/raw/README.md?current_user=<owner>&?current_user=&ref=main , and the backend reads the first  current_user  value. 
 
 Why it returns private data (backend, OpenCSGs/csghub-server @ v2.6.0-ce) 
 
  api/middleware/authenticator.go   isValidApiToken : when the bearer token equals the configured  APIToken , it reads  c.Query("current_user")  and sets it as the acting principal with no credential proof. 
  api/router/api.go : the model, code, and space  resolve  /  raw  file routes have no login middleware. The dataset equivalents add  middleware.MustLogin() , so datasets are not reachable through this path. 
  component/repo.go   AllowReadAccessRepo  denies an empty username on a private repository and otherwise calls  CheckUserRepoPermission , which resolves the name with  userStore.FindByUsername  (name only, no credential) and grants the read when the ReBAC check allows it, which it does for the owner or a member. 
 
 Net effect: a private model, code, or space file is served when  current_user  names the owner or a member, and denied when it is empty. 
 Impact 
 Unauthenticated read of private repository file contents (models, codes, spaces) of other users and organizations. This includes source files, configuration, data files, and any secret accidentally committed to a private repository. This is a GET path, no write or RCE is claimed. Datasets are not affected. 
 Suggested fix 
 
 Percent-encode every path segment and build the query with  net/url   Values.Encode , so a file path cannot introduce or override a query parameter. Apply to both  DownloadFile  and  DownloadFileRaw . 
 Stop falling back to the administrative server key for user-facing file reads. Resolve the acting user from the verified session server-side and always use the per-user backend method, or reject anonymous requests for non-public repositories. 
 Add an authentication guard to the resolve route so anonymous callers reach only public content. 
 On the backend, treat  current_user  on service-key calls as a privileged assertion signed by the portal rather than a plain query parameter. 
 
 Details 
 Full write-up with the request-by-request trace:  https://hackmd.io/@hieund/csghub-private-repo-file-read-idor  
 Reported by hieuPenguinnn (github.com/hieuPenguinnn). Review was static source analysis against the v2.6.0-ce tags of both repositories, no live deployment was contacted.                  Activity                 zhendi   commented   on   Nov 1, 2026            zhendi      on Nov 1, 2026           Collaborator       More actions          Thanks for the detailed report and the responsible disclosure. 
 We’ve received this and are reviewing it internally against our current codebase and supported versions. We can’t confirm or deny the issue at this stage, but we’ll follow up here as soon as the review is complete. 
 If we need further clarification or reproduction details, we’ll reach out. In the meantime, please avoid publicly exploiting or further discussing the specifics outside this issue. 
 Thanks again for bringing this to our attention.                  Sign up for free       to join this conversation on GitHub.   Already have an account? An Agent Harness for Embodied Manipulation

[![Project Page](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project%20Page-auriga.stelledge.com-0A66C2.svg)](https://auriga.stelledge.com/) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Videos%20%26%20Rollouts-008080.svg)](https://auriga.stelledge.com/demos.html) [![Tech Report](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tech%20Report-PDF-B31B1B.svg)](docs/Auriga-Technical-Report.pdf) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Python 3.12](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.12-3776AB.svg)](environment.yml) [![Node.js 22](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-22-339933.svg)](web/package.json) [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Tech Report (PDF)](docs/Auriga-Technical-Report.pdf) · [Demo](https://auriga.stelledge.com/demos.html) · [Documentation](docs/README.md) · [Contributor Guide](AGENTS.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Citation](#-citation)
--- **Auriga** is an agent harness for embodied robot manipulation. A model runs in a persistent Codex session, looks at camera images and robot state, plans, calls tools, writes and reviews small helper programs, and moves a robot—while the harness owns the execution boundary, the run state, and the evidence record. The default environment is the [RoboDojo](https://robodojo-benchmark.com/) simulation benchmark with a dual-arm **ARX X5**. Instead of hardcoding task-specific scripts or handing control to an open-loop policy, Auriga keeps **the model in the lead** and treats tools as scene-neutral instruments: - **Deliberate before moving**: The model localizes objects in 3D via calibrated multi-view geometry and previews multi-stage dual-arm trajectories while the world is paused. - **Closed-loop execution**: Every physical action goes through a single gateway (`Harness.execute`) that checks stage tolerances and grip guards in real time, pausing immediately on stalls or slips and returning fresh visual + state receipts so the model can recover in place.

--- ## Architecture

A run is an **observe → decide → act → feedback** loop: 1. Before its first physical move, the model submits a short task plan (`task_plan`). 2. `robot_action(action="preview")` plans a batch of stages (single or dual arm, gripper moves, inter-arm dependencies, and optional checkpoints) without advancing the simulator. 3. `robot_action(action="execute", plan_id=...)` runs the cached plan through [`Harness.execute`](auriga/runtime/harness.py) and monitors arrival tolerances and grip guards. 4. In RoboDojo, simulated physics is paused while the model thinks and only advances through actions or explicit `robot_wait` calls. Task scores come strictly from the native evaluator. --- ## Benchmark Results Mean Score (0–100) and Success Rate (SR) on the 42-task [RoboDojo](https://robodojo-benchmark.com/) benchmark against representative baselines: | Method | Type | Average (Score / SR) | Generalization | Precision | Long-Horizon | Memory | Open | | :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | WALL-OSS-1.0-lite | VLA | 42.6 / 35.0% | 46.7 | 38.2 | 49.9 | 57.4 | 20.8 | | GO-3 Nano Preview | Agent + WAM | 61.9 / 56.4% | 36.5 | **78.7** | **68.2** | 64.5 | 61.7 | | RoboProbe *(Ref. Harness)* | Agent | 29.0 / 22.5% | 33.4 | 12.7 | 21.5 | 43.0 | 34.4 | | HexaShell-Preview | Agent | 53.2 / 46.9% | 39.2 | 41.3 | 42.9 | 84.5 | 58.0 | | PyRUA-Lean | Agent | 55.3 / 50.4% | 48.3 | 44.8 | 54.3 | 68.4 | 60.6 | | **Auriga (Ours)** | **Agent** | **64.0 / 57.7%** | **52.9** | 46.3 | 62.1 | **93.4** | **65.4** | --- ## Tools Ten core tools are visible upfront; the rest load on demand through native Codex tool search. Each tool declares its input/output schema, physical units (`m`, `rad`, `deg`, `s`), defaults, and bounds in [`auriga/runtime/tools/definitions.py`](auriga/runtime/tools/definitions.py). | Tool | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | | `task_plan` | Submit and revise the task plan and attention list; re-injected before each decision. | | `robot_observe` | Current camera images plus joint / end-effector / gripper state; optional zoomed ROI crops. | | `robot_information`, `robot_capabilities` | Robot structure, URDF, camera calibration, native geometry, and runtime capabilities. | | `robot_action` | Preview, execute, and inspect single- or dual-arm stage batches. | | `robot_wait` | Advance simulation to watch motion or let objects settle. | | `robot_action_status` | Query the original request and execution receipt of an action. | | `program_run`, `program_status` | Run closed-loop helper or numeric programs; review the physical actions they request. | | `geometry_query`, `robot_contact_overlay` | Calibrated 3D geometry (stereo triangulation, pixel-to-plane) and gripper contact overlays. | | `vision_compare` | Measure local visual changes between two observations. | | `history_*` | Inspect past actions, trajectories, and observations; attach annotations. | | `operation_memory` | Query or record operating experience within the episode and across tasks. | | *Optional*: `robotic_view`, `stereo_guide`, `vision_review`, `depth_query`, `robot_policy_step` | Wrist-camera viewpoint solver, epipolar guide, auxiliary visual review, RGB-D queries (explicit depth condition only), and local $\pi_{0.5}$ policy step. | See [Unified Actions & Program Review](docs/development/unified-actions.md) and [Tool Contracts & Plugins](docs/development/tool-plugins.md). --- ## Requirements & Installation ### Prerequisites - **OS & GPU**: Linux `x86_64` and an NVIDIA GPU capable of running Isaac Sim 5.1. - **Conda / Mamba**: [Miniforge](https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge) (`mamba`). The project uses a single conda environment named `Auriga` (Python 3.12, see [`environment.yml`](environment.yml)); do not create a `.venv`. - **Node.js**: Node.js 22 and `npm` to build the Web UI. - **RoboDojo**: RoboDojo with Isaac Sim, IsaacLab, and task assets, pinned and patched as described in [RoboDojo Environment Setup](docs/development/robodojo-setup.md) (runs in its own interpreter). - **Codex Home**: `~/.codex` (by default) with credentials for a Responses-compatible model provider. The default model is `gpt-6.1-sol` with reasoning effort `high`; the Codex SDK/CLI version is pinned in `requirements.lock.txt`. - **Optional VGGT Service**: The [VGGT perception service](services/vggt_height/README.md) (`http://127.0.0.1:8331`) provides 3D object tables, point clouds, and height estimates. If the service is not running, those attachments are marked unavailable and the run continues; set `"external_perception": false` to disable it. ### Install ```bash git clone https://github.com/lose4578/Auriga.git cd Auriga # 1. Create the Auriga conda environment mamba env create -f environment.yml # 2. Build the Web Workbench & Experiment Library UI npm --prefix web ci && npm --prefix web run build # 3. Run CPU checks (no GPU, simulator, or model needed) mamba run -n Auriga python -m unittest discover -s tests ``` --- ## Configuration Settings merge in order: [`configs/auriga.json`](configs/auriga.json) → `configs/auriga.local.json` (git-ignored) → `--config ` → CLI flags. Put machine-specific paths (RoboDojo interpreter/checkout, Codex home, model) in `configs/auriga.local.json`: ```json { "version": 1, "model": { "name": "gpt-6.1-sol", "reasoning_effort": "high", "codex_home": "~/.codex" }, "features": { "sandbox_enabled": false, "external_perception": true }, "paths": { "runs_dir": "runs", "archive_root": "~/exp/auriga", "robodojo_python": "/path/to/miniforge3/envs/robodojo/bin/python", "robodojo_root": "/path/to/RoboDojo" } } ``` Inspect the effective merged configuration without starting any service: ```bash mamba run -n Auriga python -m auriga.apps.gateway --print-config ``` See the [Configuration Guide](docs/development/configuration.md) and the [annotated example](configs/auriga.example.json) for all fields. --- ## Quick Start ### 1. Run a Single Episode Pick a free GPU and a new run directory: ```bash mamba run -n Auriga python -u -m auriga.apps.gateway \ --benchmark --task general_pickup --seed 0 --layout-id 0 \ --gpu 0 --port 8767 --run-dir runs/my-first-task ``` Open **** to watch the cameras, native Codex terminal, action previews, and run record. ### 2. Replay, Browse & Render ```bash # Read-only replay of an archived run directory (no GPU, no model) mamba run -n Auriga python -m auriga.apps.gateway --replay --run-dir runs/my-first-task --port 8767 # Experiment library: browse runs, comparisons, and replays at http://127.0.0.1:8780 mamba run -n Auriga python -m auriga.apps.library # Re-simulate an archived trajectory and render HD videos (needs simulator, never calls the model) mamba run -n Auriga python -m auriga.apps.replay.hd_replay --source-run runs/my-first-task --output runs/my-first-task-hd ``` ### 3. Batch Evaluation Batch evaluation uses a manifest and the queue (`python -m auriga.apps.evaluation.queue`). Fixed benchmark suites in [`benchmarks/`](benchmarks) generate manifests: - [`gpt-as-policy-10`](benchmarks/gpt-as-policy-10/README.md): 10 tasks × 5 scenes (50 cases). - [`robodojo-42-15`](benchmarks/robodojo-42-15/README.md): All 42 official tasks × 15 scenes (630 cases). See the [Running Guide](docs/development/running.md) for session resume, interactive control, batch scheduling, reports, and audits. --- ## Security Generated code runs as your OS user by default (`features.sandbox_enabled=false`): native Codex commands, sub-agents, and `program_run` have your user's file and network access, and only the harness's application-level boundaries apply (observation filtering, action admission, program review). On Linux hosts with `bubblewrap`, Landlock ABI ≥ 4, and `libseccomp`, you can enable OS isolation with `{"version": 1, "features": {"sandbox_enabled": true}}`; startup fails explicitly instead of downgrading when isolation is unavailable. See [Code Execution Sandbox](docs/development/configuration.md#code-execution-sandbox). Keep credentials in `~/.codex`, never in the repository. --- ## Repository Layout ```text auriga/ Python package, six layers; module imports only point downward core/ contracts, configuration, information boundary, storage, model-facing presentation robot/ robot model and calibration, motion contracts and planners, RoboDojo backend perception/ image measurement, overlays, optional external perception, RGB-D, scene store cortex/ Codex session and sandbox, actor startup context, turn supervision runtime/ Harness, robot_action orchestration, tool registry and plugins, programs, policy bridge apps/ gateway/workbench, experiment library, evaluation queue, HD replay, reference baseline web/ workbench and experiment-library frontend (built into the package) configs/ default configuration, full example, image settings, presets, pricing cards benchmarks/ fixed benchmark groups (cases and partitions) scripts/ packaging, benchmark-group generator, compatibility entry points, probes services/ optional VGGT 3D perception service contracts/ protocol fixtures used by tests tests/ CPU contract and regression tests third_party/ pinned third-party material with licenses (Codex model catalog, RoboProbe) docs/ development guides, design documents, and perception notes ``` **Code tour**: [`auriga/apps/gateway/cli.py`](auriga/apps/gateway/cli.py) builds a [`Workbench`](auriga/apps/gateway/workbench.py), which starts the Codex session ([`auriga/cortex/session/codex.py`](auriga/cortex/session/codex.py)) and the [`Harness`](auriga/runtime/harness.py). Tools are declared in [`auriga/runtime/tools/definitions.py`](auriga/runtime/tools/definitions.py) and assembled in [`auriga/runtime/tools/builtins.py`](auriga/runtime/tools/builtins.py); `robot_action` lives in [`auriga/runtime/actions/unified_actions.py`](auriga/runtime/actions/unified_actions.py). Physical execution goes from [`Harness.execute`](auriga/runtime/harness.py) over [`auriga/robot/backends/robodojo/robot_process.py`](auriga/robot/backends/robodojo/robot_process.py) to [`auriga/robot/backends/robodojo/robot_worker.py`](auriga/robot/backends/robodojo/robot_worker.py) inside the RoboDojo interpreter. --- ## Where to Start | You want to… | Read | | :--- | :--- | | Run tasks and benchmarks | [Running Guide](docs/development/running.md), [Configuration](docs/development/configuration.md), [RoboDojo Setup](docs/development/robodojo-setup.md) | | Understand how a call flows | [Implementation Architecture](docs/development/architecture.md), [Shared Protocol](docs/design/shared-protocol.md) | | Add or change a tool | [Tool Contracts & Plugins](docs/development/tool-plugins.md), [Extension Guide](docs/development/extensions.md) | | Add a robot or environment | [Robot & Environment Integration](docs/development/robot-environment-integration.md), [Backend Boundaries](docs/development/robot-backend-boundaries.md) | | Know what the model may see | [Actor Information Boundary](docs/development/actor-information-boundary.md) | | Work on 3D perception | [obs3d](docs/obs3d.md), [object_table](docs/object_table.md), [scene3d](docs/scene3d.md), [vggt_height](docs/vggt_height.md) | | Work on the Web UI | [web/README.md](web/README.md) | | Browse and replay experiments | [Experiment Library](docs/development/experiment-library.md), [HD Replay](docs/development/hd-replay.md) | | Contribute | [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [Validation Guide](docs/development/validation.md), [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) | Full index: [docs/README.md](docs/README.md). --- ## License & Third-Party Material Auriga is released under the [MIT License](LICENSE). [`third_party/`](third_party) keeps upstream licenses and provenance for vendored material (Codex model catalog and RoboProbe reference code, both Apache-2.0). RoboDojo, Isaac Sim, IsaacLab, cuRobo, and model weights are not distributed with this repository. --- ## 🌟 Citation If you use Auriga in your research or engineering work, please cite the repository: ```bibtex @software{auriga2026code, title = {Auriga: An Agent Harness for Embodied Manipulation}, author = {{StellarEdge AI Technical Team}}, year = {2026}, url = {https://github.com/lose4578/Auriga}, version = {0.2.0}, license = {MIT} } ```

      Title: Auriga Technical Report: A Task-Agnostic Agent Harness for Zero-Shot Embodied Manipulation 
      Authors:  Chengcheng Wang ,  Yuheng Shi ,  Siyu Xu ,  Yutong Wang ,  Jinjing Zhao ,  Chenghao Xia ,  Jinqi Liao ,  Jiankun Peng ,  Ligong Bi ,  Yuechuan Ma ,  Jiaqi Liu ,  Wenbo Wang ,  Zijian Wang ,  Yuemin Wu ,  Minjing Dong ,  Xiu Su ,  Tao Huang ,  Jianyuan Guo ,  Chengbin Du ,  Yunke Wang ,  Chang Xu               View a PDF of the paper titled Auriga Technical Report: A Task-Agnostic Agent Harness for Zero-Shot Embodied Manipulation, by Chengcheng Wang and 20 other authors 
     View PDF 
     HTML (experimental) 



     
             Abstract: Vision-language models can interpret instructions and plan manipulation tasks, yet struggle when acting directly as robot policies. On RoboDojo, a large planning-execution gap separates high-level task decisions from physical execution: removing arm execution raises GPT-6 Astra's success rate from 22.5% under the reference control interface to 76.2%. We present Auriga, a task-agnostic agent harness that closes 68.3% of this gap in zero-shot manipulation without target-task trials or resets. In Auriga, the model makes all task decisions over an explicit task belief and acts through either direct tool calls or synthesized multi-step Python programs, while the harness supplies calibrated 3D measurements, finger-referenced dual-arm control, and a single admission gateway to the robot. Before motion, the model inspects a visual trajectory preview while simulation is paused; during execution, the harness checks declared stage tolerances and grasp bounds, stopping the robot on divergence and returning the measured discrepancy for in-place recovery. Developed across 13 cross-task capability iterations and frozen for evaluation, Auriga ranks first on the RoboDojo leaderboard with a 57.7% success rate (64.0 Score), more than doubling the reference harness on the same model, and remains first under scene randomization while learned policies drop by up to 33.9%. On RoboCasa365, the same frozen harness reaches a 73.2% success rate, outperforming VLA-assisted agents by up to 23.1% on composite tasks.

        Architecture  架构  
        Decision, capability, admission  决策、能力与执行准入  
       Cortex maintains the task belief and chooses each action. General tools provide measurements and motion previews; one admission gateway executes the previewed trajectory, checks each movement stage, and returns evidence for the next decision.  Cortex 维护任务信念并选择动作。通用工具提供测量与运动预览；所有物理动作经过同一准入网关，执行预览轨迹、逐阶段验证，并返回证据供模型继续决策。 
       
      
     
     
       
         
       
      
        Direct and program-generated motions share the same gateway. Dashed paths store and retrieve evidence; task belief remains the model’s revisable interpretation. The workbench supports inspection and replay.  直接动作与程序生成的动作共用准入网关。虚线路径用于记录和检索证据；任务信念是模型可修订的判断。工作台提供查看与回放。  
     
     
       
         01  Observe  观察  
         02  Belief  信念  
         03  Preview  预览  
         04  Execute  执行  
         05  Feedback  反馈  
       
       

         STEP 01  Observe & measure  Calibrated RGB views and measured robot state ground the next decision. Tools add 3D object estimates and geometric measurements with explicit reliability indicators.  Observation, measurement, retrieval, and preview leave the simulated world paused.    步骤 01  观察与测量  标定的 RGB 视图与实测机器人状态为决策提供依据；工具补充带有可靠性说明的物体三维估计与几何测量。  观察、测量、检索与预览均不推进仿真时间。   
         STEP 02  Maintain task belief  Before the first physical action, Cortex submits a task belief: a plan, an attention list of uncertainties, and a ledger of task-critical premises.  Premises remain pending, supported, contradicted, or unknown according to evidence. The latest belief survives context compaction; detailed evidence stays retrievable.    步骤 02  维护任务信念  首次物理动作前，Cortex 提交任务信念：计划、记录不确定性的关注列表，以及记录关键前提的账本。  前提根据证据标记为待验证、有支持、被反驳或未知。上下文压缩后保留最新信念，详细证据仍可检索。   
         STEP 03  Preview before acting  Every requested motion, including one generated by a program, is compiled into a trajectory preview with paths and stage timing before it can execute.  The model reviews the preview by default. It may skip a separate review turn, but execution still uses the cached previewed trajectory without replanning.    步骤 03  执行前预览  每个运动请求，包括程序生成的动作，都先编译为包含路径与阶段时长的轨迹预览。  模型默认检查预览，也可跳过单独的检查轮次；执行仍使用已预览的缓存轨迹，不重新规划。   
         STEP 04  Execute & verify  The gateway executes the cached trajectory and checks the reached pose at the end of each movement stage. A deviation beyond the model’s declared tolerance stops the remaining stages.  Model-placed checkpoints pause for fresh observations, optionally triggered by gripper aperture. Completed motion is not undone.    步骤 04  执行与验证  网关执行缓存轨迹，在每个运动阶段结束时检查到达位姿。偏差超出模型声明的容差时，停止后续阶段。  模型设置的检查点会暂停执行并返回新观察，也可由夹爪开度条件触发；已完成的运动不会撤销。   
         STEP 05  Assess & revise  The receipt reports completed and unexecuted stages, measured deviations, and fresh views. Cortex diagnoses the outcome and chooses whether to continue, gather evidence, or preview a revised motion.  Outcomes update the task belief and evidence record. The benchmark evaluator determines task success independently of motion completion or normal program termination.    步骤 05  评估与修正  回执报告已完成与未执行阶段、实测偏差和新视图。Cortex 诊断结果，决定继续、收集证据，或预览修订后的动作。  动作结果更新任务信念与证据记录。任务是否成功由基准评估器独立判断，区别于运动完成或程序正常退出。   
     
     
     
    
    Stage loop  阶段闭环   The gateway stops at excessive pose error, a failed grasp check, or a model checkpoint.  网关在位姿偏差超限、抓取检查失败或模型检查点处停止。     Action loop  动作闭环   The model diagnoses each outcome and chooses a continuation, a revised motion, or another observation.  模型诊断动作结果，选择继续、修订动作或再次观察。     Belief loop  信念闭环   Evidence revises the ledger and plan; contradicted premises lead to a different approach.  证据更新账本与计划；前提被反驳时，模型调整方案。   
     
     
       
           Design principles  设计原则  
          Four commitments  四条原则   
         The model decides what to do, tools provide the capabilities, and the harness owns the boundary between decision and physical execution.  由模型决定做什么，工具提供能力，框架负责决策与物理执行之间的边界。 
       
         01   Explicit task belief  显式任务信念   Keep goals, unresolved questions, and supported premises in a compact working state; check them against retrievable evidence.  将目标、待解决问题和有支持的前提保存在精简的工作状态中，并通过可检索证据核对。    02   Preview is the execution contract  预览约束执行   Direct and program-generated motions execute the cached previewed trajectory. Inspection changes no simulated state.  直接动作与程序生成的动作执行已预览的缓存轨迹，预览检查不改变仿真状态。    03   Verify each movement stage  逐阶段验证   Declared tolerances and selective observation checkpoints expose errors before later stages compound them.  通过声明的容差与按需设置的观察检查点，及时暴露误差，避免后续阶段放大问题。    04   The model chooses recovery  模型决定恢复方式   The gateway stops and reports; Cortex interprets the evidence and changes the action or task belief.  网关负责停止和报告，Cortex 解释证据，调整动作或任务信念。   
     
     
     
     
       
           Control paradigms  控制范式  
          Three ways to put a model on a robot  让模型控制机器人的三种方式   
         The paradigms differ in who decides, what reaches the actuators, and how failures are noticed and repaired.  三种范式的区别在于：由谁决策、什么指令到达执行器，以及如何发现和修复失败。 
       
       
              
          
               
            (a)  Action model (VLA)  动作模型（VLA）  
            (b)  General model, direct control  通用模型直接控制  
            (c) ·  ours  本方法  Auriga 
          
         
             Decides  决策  
              A learned policy maps images and the instruction to actions.  由学习得到的策略将图像和指令映射为动作。  
              A general model chooses the next action at each step (e.g. GPT Direct).  通用模型在每一步选择下一个动作（如 GPT Direct）。  
              A persistent Cortex session maintains task belief and retrieves episode evidence.  持续的 Cortex 会话维护任务信念，并检索本局证据。   
             Executes  执行  
              Predicted action chunks go straight to the robot.  预测的动作块直接下发给机器人。  
              One tool call, one robot step.  一次工具调用对应机器人的一步动作。  
              Direct or program-generated motions use one gateway and the cached previewed trajectory.  直接动作或程序生成的动作通过同一网关，执行已预览的缓存轨迹。   
             Feedback  反馈  
              Implicit, through the next camera frame.  隐式反馈，通过下一帧相机图像获得。  
              A new observation after each call.  每次调用后获得一次新的观察。  
              Fresh views, pose deviations, completed stages, and remaining stages in each execution receipt.  执行回执包含新视图、位姿偏差、已完成阶段与剩余阶段。   
             Recovery  恢复  
              Bounded by what the training data covers.  受限于训练数据的覆盖范围。  
              Re-decided at each call from the new frame; no plan preview or execution receipt.  每次调用根据新图像重新决策；没有计划预览和执行回执。  
              The gateway stops on failed checks; Cortex diagnoses, resumes, or revises its action and belief.  检查失败时网关停止，Cortex 负责诊断、继续，或修订动作与信念。   
         
       
     
     
   
 

 
 
   
      
       
        Tool layer  工具层  
        Measure, act, compute, recall  测量、动作、计算与检索

Deliberation leaves the simulated world paused; only physical requests advance it through the admission gateway.  通用能力将观察转化为带有可靠性说明的测量，将模型决策转化为可检查的动作。思考与查询期间仿真保持暂停，只有经过准入网关的物理请求才推进世界。
